prompt: What is the castle-and-moat model?

choices.text: Outside hostile, inside trusted
choices.why: Right. The firewall is the wall in between.

choices.text: Two firewalls in a row from different vendors
choices.why: That is one way to build a DMZ.

choices.text: Keeping servers in a physically guarded room
choices.why: That is a physical control, not the network model.

choices.text: A network with no firewall
choices.why: The model is built around one firewall.

prompt: Which change does the lesson call the important one for why the perimeter cannot stand alone?

choices.text: Staff working from home, outside the wall every evening
choices.why: A reason, and not the one the lesson singles out.

choices.text: Email moving to the cloud, outside the wall by design
choices.why: A reason, and not the one singled out.

choices.text: Firewalls becoming cheaper
choices.why: Price is not one of the three.

choices.text: Attackers get in without crossing it
choices.why: Right. An inside built on trust then offers them everything.

prompt: Why does the lesson say NAT is not a perimeter control?

choices.text: Its blocking is a side effect, not a design
choices.why: Right. It looks like a firewall and was not built as one.

choices.text: NAT lets every connection from the internet straight in
choices.why: Unsolicited connections usually do not get in through NAT.

choices.text: NAT only exists in the cloud
choices.why: Most home routers do it.

choices.text: The lab uses NAT instead of rules
choices.why: The lab has no NAT at all.

prompt: What belongs in a DMZ?

choices.text: The database the shop's pages read from
choices.why: Data stays inside; the DMZ asks for it through one port.

choices.text: Services the internet must reach
choices.why: Right. Web, inbound mail, public DNS, a VPN gateway.

choices.text: The staff's laptops
choices.why: Nobody on the internet should reach those.

choices.text: The administrators' machines
choices.why: They belong in their own management segment.

prompt: Order the zones by how much the firewall trusts what comes from them, least first.
trap: The internet reaches only the DMZ; the DMZ reaches one port inside; the servers are where the data is.

prompt: www is compromised. Under the lesson's rules, what can its attacker reach?

choices.text: Everything inside, since www is a trusted server
choices.why: The DMZ is not trusted; that is its point.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: One path is allowed on purpose.

choices.text: The database's port 5432
choices.why: Right. What it was allowed to do anyway, and no more.

choices.text: The office, to ask staff for passwords
choices.why: The DMZ may not reach the office.

prompt: Two firewalls in a row, outer and inner, cost more than one with three legs. What does the second shape buy?

choices.text: Faster connections from the internet
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: No need for rules on the inner one
choices.why: Both need rules.

choices.text: A second layer, more so if the vendors differ
choices.why: Right. Different reasons to fail.

choices.text: A DMZ that may also hold the database, since it is better protected
choices.why: Data never goes in the DMZ.

prompt: Match each word probe prints to what it means.

pairs.right: the machine said nothing listens there

prompt: Before any rule, www → db:22 said refused. What did that tell an attacker on www?

choices.text: That the firewall blocked port 22
choices.why: A firewall drop looks like blocked, not refused.

choices.text: That db exists and runs nothing on 22
choices.why: Right. The network delivered the attempt and the machine answered.

choices.text: That db is switched off
choices.why: A switched-off machine does not answer at all.

choices.text: That the database is encrypted
choices.why: Nothing about encryption shows in a probe.

prompt: An attacker moving from one compromised machine to the next inside a network is doing ___ movement.
In the rules file, what does policy drop do?

choices.text: Drops whatever no rule accepted
choices.why: Right. That is default deny.

choices.text: Drops replies to allowed connections
choices.why: ct state established,related lets those back.

choices.text: Deletes the rules when the firewall restarts
choices.why: It is about packets, not the file.

choices.text: Drops packets from the DMZ and accepts the rest
choices.why: It applies to anything no rule accepted, from any zone.

prompt: Why is default deny the only policy the lesson calls safe when somebody adds a machine?
hint: What happens to the machine nobody thought about?

choices.text: Because it logs every connection
choices.why: Logging is a different control.

choices.text: Forgetting a machine fails closed
choices.why: Right. Forgetting fails closed.

choices.text: Because it is faster than listing what to block
choices.why: Speed is not the argument.

choices.text: Because new machines are always in the DMZ
choices.why: They go wherever somebody plugs them in.

prompt: After the rules, www → laptop:22 changed from refused to blocked. What is the gain?
hint: What can a compromised www learn now?

choices.text: Port 22 on laptop is now encrypted
choices.why: Nothing was encrypted.

choices.text: The laptop now runs an SSH server
choices.why: Nothing was started on the laptop.

choices.text: No difference, since nothing listened on 22 either way
choices.why: The attempt no longer arrives, which hides what the laptop runs.

choices.text: www no longer maps the laptop's ports
choices.why: Right. Lateral movement starts with that map.

prompt: How many accept rules for new connections did zones.nft need for the shop's three-sentence policy?
hint: Not counting the line for replies.

prompt: A rule set was tested only from the office laptop, where its author sits. What does the lesson say about that test?

choices.text: It is enough, since the office is the most used zone
choices.why: Use is not what the test is about.

choices.text: Nothing about the internet or a compromised server
choices.why: Right. Test from every zone.

choices.text: It is invalid unless an auditor watches
choices.why: No such rule.

choices.text: It proves default deny works
choices.why: It proves only what the office can reach.

prompt: Match each segment to why it is kept apart.

pairs.right: nobody controls what runs on them
they hold the keys to everything else
email and browsing are how attackers get in

prompt: Traffic between two machines inside the network is called what?

choices.text: North-south
choices.why: That is traffic crossing the perimeter.

choices.text: East-west
choices.why: Right. The perimeter never sees it.

choices.text: Inbound
choices.why: Inbound is from outside in.

choices.text: Perimeter traffic
choices.why: It never touches the perimeter.

prompt: A camera with old firmware sits on the same segment as the database. What does the lesson recommend first?
hint: Its weakness should stay its own.

choices.text: Patch the database so the camera cannot harm it
choices.why: The camera's weakness is what needs containing.

choices.text: Remove the firewall rules so the camera works
choices.why: That flattens the network further.

choices.text: Its own segment, reaching only what it needs
choices.why: Right. Guests and devices get their own zone.

choices.text: Put the camera in the DMZ so the internet can watch it
choices.why: The DMZ is for services the internet must reach.

prompt: Which of these does the lab's rule set allow? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: outside → www:80
choices.why: Rule 1.

choices.text: www → db:5432
choices.why: Rule 2.

choices.text: laptop → db:5432
choices.why: Rule 3 does not include the servers.

choices.text: www → laptop:22
choices.why: The DMZ may not reach the office.

prompt: The shop adds a new server for invoices on the servers segment and changes nothing else. Who can reach it?
hint: Rule 2 names one address and one port.

choices.text: www, since the DMZ reaches the servers
choices.why: Rule 2 names db's address and port 5432 only.

choices.text: Nobody, until a rule allows it
choices.why: Right. Default deny covers the machine nobody thought about.

choices.text: The internet, since nothing blocks it
choices.why: policy drop blocks it.

choices.text: The office, through rule 3
choices.why: Rule 3 reaches the internet and the DMZ only.
